01/On court, on the pitch, in the league

Padel, hosting
& FPL

8 mo
playing padel
1–2x
per week
Right
court side · left-handed

Started padel with my wife, and it stuck — Adidas Metalbone Carbon 2026 in hand, right side is home. Padel is also how I met most of the people I now hang out with outside of padel, via two regular reclubs: Smashoora and Sunmory Padel Club. Pickleball's the newer thing — three sessions in with Amartha so far, a nice change of pace from padel.

Football too: monthly mini-soccer at Amartha (I play striker), plus full-pitch games with college friends who run with another group, SMB (Senang Main Bola).

I co-run a padel reclub, Courterra Club, with my wife and a college friend — he hosts regularly in North Jakarta, I've hosted once or twice in South Jakarta. Trying to make it a habit, still figuring out the hosting model.

And tied to football: I play FPL — Fantasy Premier League. Draft a squad of real Premier League players, score points off their real-world goals, assists, clean sheets.

02/What I load up after hours

Games I play,
badge I wear

Valorant is the competitive one — FPS with ability kits layered on top of pure aim, which is what keeps it interesting. FIFA / EAFC has been a constant since FIFA 12 through EAFC 25 (EAFC 26 is bought, not touched yet) — couch sessions with friends, classroom sessions back in high school, and during peak COVID, full Pro Clubs runs where everyone controls one player on the pitch.

Yu-Gi-Oh Duel Links on phone or iPad scratches the same itch as the real card game, just compressed to a 3-monster, 3-spell/trap field. Current rotation, whenever setup and mood line up: Rogue Galaxy on PCSX2 — a PS2-era action RPG I owned back in the day. Not turn-based, deep mechanics, and my favorite bit — fusing two weapons into one upgraded weapon.

  • Valorant
  • FIFA → EAFC
  • Yu-Gi-Oh Duel Links
  • Rogue Galaxy (PCSX2)

Valorant and its esports scene is also how I met content creator / coach Sleepy — which led to me becoming a Discord moderator for Paper Rex. The job: watching chat, kicking and banning spam, keeping match threads in order when takes get out of hand — and hosting Friday mabar (group play) sessions in the Paper Rex Discord.

03/Passports and setlists

Traveling
& concerts

Family trips abroad go back to elementary school — Singapore most years. Didn't understand the pull then; understand it a bit more now. Countries visited so far: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Australia, Japan, Korea, Hong Kong, France, UK, Scotland, Spain, Germany, Hungary, Switzerland, Austria, Czech Republic. Most likely to go back to: Japan. If I ever relocated for work, Singapore or Malaysia — close culturally, large Indonesian community.

Lately, travel and concerts overlap. Trips to Singapore have lined up with Wallows and Big Time Rush, and I'm taking leave soon to catch Alex Warren. Locally, I'm a big .feast and Hindia fan and go whenever they play an album release show. Most memorable: a .feast show with a big group of friends — pure chaos, in a good way.

04/Currently light on watchlist, heavy on recs

What I'm watching

Not deep in a series right now, but if you ask me for a recommendation, it's always one of these two:

"Person of Interest" — a hacker and an AI that flags who's about to kill, or be killed. Plays like a crime procedural, just running on different jurisdiction rules than the usual show.
"Leverage" — a crew building elaborate cons and heists against people who deserve it. The scheming is the show; the ending is always the good guys winning.
05/Why frontend, what's hard, what's home

Work, passion
& family

Went frontend because it's the visible layer — testing a backend feature back then meant standing up the frontend first, which was really a sign the BE onboarding wasn't quite there. That, plus a frontend need at my previous company, sealed it.

Biggest challenge is personal, not technical: I'm a side-quest person before a main-quest person — true in games, true at the office. Working on flipping that order — main quest first, side quests after.

The passion I haven't gotten to yet: work with a visible, national-scale outcome — something where success looks like poverty numbers actually moving. Alongside that, the practical target is a senior leadership role with pay that covers a good life plus family, and a schedule that still fits padel in the morning and again at night around a real day of work impact.

At home, it's the two of us — my wife's a college friend, same industry (IT), so work conversations land easily. We don't overlap on everything: she's not actually a .feast or Hindia fan, we just make it work. Currently trying for a first kid — appreciate the good thoughts.
